title: Rejection Causes and Recollection Time for Specimens Taken at Halverson Collection Visits
content:
For Laboratory Test Orders, the cause of the most recent specimen rejection lengthens the recollection window when the rejected specimen was taken at a Halverson collection visit. Such a visit is a visit of Specimen Collection Appointments recorded for the accession with the status *collected*.

## The rule

- **Transport-related cause.** The most recent rejection reason is *stability exceeded* or *leaked in transit*, and the rejected specimen was collected at a Halverson collection visit recorded for the accession with status *collected*. The recollection window is lengthened by **7 days**.
- **Collection-related cause.** The most recent rejection reason is *hemolyzed*, *quantity not sufficient*, *unlabeled or mislabeled* or *wrong container*, and the rejected specimen was collected at such a Halverson collection visit. The recollection window is lengthened by **3 days**.
- **No such visit.** A specimen not collected at a Halverson collection visit recorded for the accession receives no rejection-cause lengthening.

## Decision table

| Most recent rejection reason | Collected visit recorded for the accession in Specimen Collection Appointments | Lengthening |
|---|---|---|
| Stability exceeded, or leaked in transit | Yes | 7 days |
| Hemolyzed, quantity not sufficient, unlabeled or mislabeled, or wrong container | Yes | 3 days |
| Any reason | No | none |

## Points of judgement

- **Only the most recent rejection counts.** An accession rejected first for hemolysis and then for leakage in transit, with its specimen taken at a collected Halverson visit, is lengthened by 7 days. The latest reason is the transport-related one.
- **One lengthening, never both.** The two causes are alternatives decided by the single most recent reason, so an accession receives 7 days, 3 days or none.
